prs.title: Make popups and top-level data: documents follow their creator for secure contexts
prs.author: annevk
prs.body:
The initial about:blank document of an auxiliary browsing context now copies its creator's top-level creation URL rather than using about:blank. It is therefore a secure context if and only if its creator is one, which is what browsers do and what web-platform-tests expects.

A top-level data: document, and anything nested in it, is no longer a secure context. This follows https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-secure-contexts/issues/69. data: documents nested in a secure context remain secure contexts.

Fixes #6369. Fixes #12091.

- [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed):
   * WebKit
   * Gecko
- [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at:
   * `secure-contexts/basic-popup-and-iframe-tests.html` and `secure-contexts/basic-popup-and-iframe-tests.https.html` cover popups.
   * Top-level data: documents are hard to test as browsers block navigating a top-level browsing context to them.

prs.title: Don't set force async to false in Fragment scripting mode
prs.author: noamr
prs.body:
In the `Fragment` scripting mode (used by `createContextualFragment()`, `setHTMLUnsafe()` and the positional `*HTMLUnsafe()` methods with `runScripts: true`, and `innerHTML`/`outerHTML`/`insertAdjacentHTML()` when a Trusted Types default policy enables `runScripts`), the HTML parser does not set the `script` element's `parser document`. Previously, it still set `force async` to false, and because `prepare the script element` only resets `force async` to true when `parser document` is non-null, external scripts without `async` kept `force async` set to false once inserted.

All three browser engines (Chromium, Gecko, and WebKit) instead leave `force async` as true in this case (`script.async` returns `true` before insertion, and external scripts without `async` execute as async once inserted).

Only set `force async` to false in `#scriptTag` when `scripting mode` is not `Fragment` (i.e., when `parser document` is set).

Fixes #13079.

   * Gecko (already matches this behavior)
   * WebKit (already matches this behavior)
